Trionyx kansaiensis
is an
extinct
species
of
softshell turtle
uncovered from the
Late Cretaceous
of
Tajikistan
and
Qyzylorda
,
Kazakhstan
.Fossil evidence from the Bissekty Formation in Uzbekistan indicate that the Trionyx Kansaiensis or a closely related species were more widely spread across Central Asia during the Late Cretaceous than research previously showed (Vitek, 2013). Other fossils from the Bostobe Formation suggest that this species lived in river and delta environments. T. Kansaiensis’ shell anatomy shows intermediate traits between very early and modern day trionychids, suggesting that it came along somewhere in the middle of the evolutionary history of the species (Vitek and Danilov, 2010).
